theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before installing an LED sign on a shop front, what should you agree first with the customer, using the drawing?
options: Its position, fixings and power supply point
Only the colour of the letters the owner likes best
Only the price the owner paid for the sign itself
Only the opening hours of the shop for customers

questions.stem: What is a "channel letter" sign?
options: A flat printed banner lit up by a floodlight on a pole
A screen that shows moving adverts
Separate hollow letters, each lit inside by LEDs
Letters painted straight onto the wall

questions.stem: Which kind of LED sign can show changing words, prices and pictures?
options: A single channel letter
A programmable LED message display
A painted, unlit lightbox
An LED strip outline

questions.stem: Most LED modules and strips used in signs run on which supply?
options: 220 V AC taken straight from the mains
110 V AC taken straight from a socket
High-voltage DC from an ignition coil
Low-voltage DC, often 12 V or 24 V

questions.stem: What does the LED driver in a sign do?
options: Changes mains AC to the low-voltage DC the LEDs need
Switches the sign on by itself at dusk and off again at dawn
Keeps rain and dust out of the sign box and its wiring
Holds the sign box firmly to the wall in strong winds

questions.stem: An LED module is marked "12 V DC". Which type of driver should feed it?
options: A constant-current driver of any voltage
A 12 V AC transformer for halogen lamps
A constant-voltage 12 V DC driver
A car battery charger set to 12 V

questions.stem: A sign uses 5 m of LED strip rated 14.4 W per metre. What is the total load?
The LEDs in a sign draw 72 W in total. Why is a driver of about 90–100 W chosen, rather than one of exactly 72 W?
options: So that the LEDs give out about twice as much light
So it is not run flat out, and so lasts longer
So that the sign can be fed straight from 220 V
So that the metal driver case needs no earth wire

questions.stem: A 12 V DC driver supplies 60 W of LEDs. Using I = P ÷ V, what current flows in its output cable?
options: 5 A

questions.stem: A long run of 12 V LED strip is bright at the start and dim at the far end. What is the most likely cause?
options: The supply frequency is set too high
The LEDs at that end are a different colour
The metal sign box has not been earthed
Voltage drop along the strip's thin tracks

questions.stem: What is a common way to cure dimming at the far end of a long LED strip run?
options: Feed power in at both ends, or along the run
Add another metre of strip to the far end
Feed the strip straight from the 220 V mains
Cut the strip and throw the dim half away

questions.stem: For the same power, why is a 24 V LED system often chosen over 12 V for a large sign?
options: It is safer to touch than a 12 V system
It can be run without any driver at all
It draws half the current, so less voltage drop
It makes the LEDs give out a whiter colour

questions.stem: What is likely to happen if the + and − wires to an LED module are swapped?
options: The module lights in a different colour
The module will not light, and may be damaged
The module lights twice as brightly as before
The driver changes its output to AC

questions.stem: What does the IP rating on an LED module or driver tell you?
options: How much power it takes from the supply
How bright it is compared with others
How long its maker's guarantee lasts
How well it keeps out dust and water

questions.stem: Which driver is a sensible choice for fitting outdoors on a Kingston shop front, where rain will reach it?
options: One rated about IP65 or higher, as the maker says
One rated IP20, which is made for indoor use
Any driver at all, if it is wrapped in a plastic bag
An indoor driver hidden just behind the sign box

questions.stem: Why is a drip loop left in a cable just before it enters a sign box?
options: So that the cable can be pulled up tight
So that the cable carries more current
So rain drips off the low point, not into the entry
So the cable can be cut shorter later on

questions.stem: How should a cable enter an outdoor sign box or driver enclosure?
options: Through a hole drilled into the top of the box lid
Through a sized gland, from below where possible
Through the gap left under the lid of the box
Through any spare hole, sealed over with tape

questions.stem: Which fixing is most suitable for holding a sign bracket to a concrete block wall?
options: Plasterboard screws driven straight in
Steel nails hammered into the blocks
A strong glue spread on the bracket
Masonry fixings of the type the maker states

questions.stem: Why must the fixing of an outdoor sign be checked with special care in Jamaica?
options: Hurricane-force winds can tear off a poorly fixed sign
Strong sun makes the sign much heavier as the years pass
Heavy rain makes the screws swell and grow
Signs are inspected only for how they look

questions.stem: When a ladder is used to reach a sign position, what angle is usually recommended?
options: About 45°, or 1 out for every 1 up
Straight up, flat against the wall
About 75°, or 1 out for every 4 up
About 30° from the ground

questions.stem: How far should a ladder used to step onto a flat roof extend above the landing point?
options: About 10 cm
About 1 m
About 3 m
It need not extend above it

questions.stem: What is the safest way to work on a sign about 4 m above a busy sidewalk?
options: From the top step of a tall stepladder, held by a friend
By leaning out of an upstairs window
From a chair set on top of a table
From a scaffold, with the area below coned off

questions.stem: Before working on the mains side of a sign's driver, what must be done?
options: Switch off, lock off, tag, and prove dead with a checked tester
Cover the sign's photocell so that the LEDs go out
Set the sign's time switch to the off position
Put on rubber gloves and work carefully with the supply still on

questions.stem: Why is an isolator switch often fitted close to an outdoor sign?
options: So that passing customers can switch it on
So that the sign flashes on and off
So it can be switched and locked off near the work
So that the driver gets less heat

questions.stem: Why must the metal frame or box of a mains-fed sign be earthed?
options: So that the LEDs shine more brightly at night
So a fault trips the supply, not leaving the frame live
So that birds and lizards do not settle on the sign box
So that the whole sign uses less power

questions.stem: Which device helps prevent shock if a fault lets current leak to earth from an outdoor sign circuit?
options: A larger fuse
A dimmer switch
A photocell
A GFCI or RCD

questions.stem: Which device switches a sign on at dusk and off at dawn without anyone touching it?
options: A photocell
A doorbell push
A thermostat
A fuse

questions.stem: A shop owner wants the sign on from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. only. Which control suits this best?
options: A photocell on its own
A dimmer on the driver
A time switch set to those hours
A push button by the door

questions.stem: Why must an LED driver not be sealed in a small box with no air space round it?
options: The LEDs would change colour
Heat builds up and shortens its life
Water would collect inside it
It would turn into a transformer

questions.stem: Why are the LED modules inside a backlit sign box spaced evenly and set back from the face?
options: To save on the length of cable used
To let air and rain flow through the box
To make the box heavier and steadier
To light the face evenly, with no bright spots

questions.stem: What is the best way to join cut lengths of LED strip in a sign?
options: Solder, or use the maker's connectors, at the cut points
Twist the bare copper ends together and leave them open
Wrap the ends together with sticky tape
Staple the two ends onto the backboard

questions.stem: Where may an LED strip be cut?
options: Anywhere along its length
Through the middle of an LED
Only at the marked cut lines
Only at the very end of the reel

questions.stem: Why does a long 12 V DC run to a sign often need a thicker cable than its power alone suggests?
options: Thick cable costs much less than thin cable
Low voltage means high current, so drop must be kept down
Thin cable may not be used outdoors at all
Thicker cable makes the LEDs shine a slightly different colour

questions.stem: Before the assessor powers a new sign from the bench supply, what should the group check?
options: That the face of the sign has been cleaned until it shines
That the photocell has been covered over
That the label on the driver has been removed
Polarity, connections and no short circuits, with a meter

questions.stem: One section of a sign stays dark while the rest lights. After switching off, what should be checked first?
options: The connections and wiring to that section
The colour of the letters in that section
The wall fixings at the far end of the sign
The customer's last electricity bill

questions.stem: How is new text usually loaded onto a programmable LED message display?
options: By rewiring the LEDs on the display panel in new shapes
By changing the driver for a larger one
With the maker's software, by cable or wireless link
By painting new letters on the face

questions.stem: Before a large sign is put up on a building facing the road, whose approval may be needed?
options: The power company's meter reader
The local authority (municipal corporation)
The company that made the LEDs
The customer's bank manager

questions.stem: Which material is often used for the face of a lit sign because it spreads the light evenly?
options: Plywood sheet
Galvanised steel
Clear window glass
Opal (milky white) acrylic

questions.stem: Why are UV-resistant cable ties and cables used outdoors in Jamaica?
options: Strong sunlight makes ordinary plastic brittle
They cost much less than ordinary ties
They can hold more weight when used indoors
They glow in the dark so they are easy to find

questions.stem: Which tool is used to check that a sign bracket is fixed straight and level?
options: A tape measure
A spirit level
A claw hammer
A multimeter

questions.stem: When drilling into concrete above head height to fix a sign, which PPE is most needed?
options: A hairnet and an apron
Sunglasses and soft shoes
Safety glasses and a dust mask
Rubber gloves and a cap

questions.stem: When the sign is finished, what should the installer give the customer?
options: Only the bill for the work
Only the empty boxes and off-cuts left over from the job
Nothing, if the sign is lit
Driver data, how to use the controls and who to call

questions.stem: Which is a sensible routine check for an outdoor LED sign?
options: Repaint the wall behind it every week to keep it fresh
Look for dark LEDs, loose fixings and water inside
Leave it alone until it stops working
Turn the driver voltage up each year

questions.stem: How should old LED modules and drivers taken out of a sign be disposed of?
options: As electronic waste, under the Centre's or local rules
Thrown in the nearest gully or river
Burned with the cardboard boxes they came in
Put in the canteen bin with the food waste at day's end

questions.stem: Why should a roadside sign not be set too bright at night?
options: It makes the LEDs run much cooler
It raises the IP rating of the sign
Glare can dazzle drivers and annoy neighbours
It changes the supply from AC to DC

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

essays.stem: Describe the planning a team should do before installing an LED sign on the front of a shop in Montego Bay.
essays.modelAnswer: First the team visits the site with the drawing and agrees with the owner where the sign goes, its size and how it will be lit and controlled. They check the wall: what it is made of, whether it is sound, and what fixings it needs. They find where the power will come from and plan the cable route, the isolator position and the driver position, out of the rain and with air round it. They check whether approval from the local authority or the landlord is needed. They choose safe access, such as a mobile scaffold, and plan barriers for the sidewalk below. Then they make a list of materials and tools: sign parts, driver of the right voltage and rating, cable, glands, fixings, sealant and test meters. Finally they check the weather forecast, as rain and wind make work at height unsafe, and agree who does each job.
markingPoints: Agrees position, size, lighting and controls with the customer, using the drawing
Checks the wall and chooses suitable fixings
Plans power point, cable route, isolator and driver position
Plans safe access and protection of the public; checks approvals
Lists materials and tools; checks weather; shares out jobs

essays.stem: A sign uses 8 m of 24 V LED strip rated 9.6 W per metre. Explain how you would choose a suitable driver, showing your working.
essays.modelAnswer: First I find the total load: 8 m × 9.6 W per metre = 76.8 W. The strip is marked 24 V DC, so I need a constant-voltage driver with a 24 V DC output; a driver of a different voltage, or a constant-current driver, would not suit it. A driver should not be run at its full rating, so I add a margin of about 20%: 76.8 × 1.2 is about 92 W, so I choose the next size up, a 100 W driver. The current in the output cable will be about 76.8 ÷ 24 = 3.2 A, so I choose cable that can carry this with little voltage drop. The sign is outdoors, so the driver must have a suitable IP rating, such as IP65 or higher, or be fitted inside a weatherproof enclosure, with space for air to keep it cool. I follow the maker's data sheet.
markingPoints: Total load = 8 × 9.6 = 76.8 W
Constant-voltage 24 V DC output to match the strip
Adds a margin (about 20%) and chooses about 100 W
Works out the current (about 3.2 A) for the cable
Suitable IP rating or enclosure, ventilation, maker's data

essays.stem: Explain what voltage drop is in an LED sign, how you would notice it, and three ways an installer can prevent it.
essays.modelAnswer: Voltage drop is the loss of voltage along a conductor because of its resistance. LED strips have thin copper tracks, and low-voltage systems carry a large current for their power, so the voltage falls along a long run. You notice it because the LEDs near the feed are bright and those at the far end are dimmer, and white LEDs may look slightly yellow or pink at the far end. To prevent it, keep each run within the length the maker allows. Feed power in at both ends, or at points along the run, using separate feed cables from the driver. Use a 24 V system instead of 12 V where possible, as it carries half the current for the same power. Use cable that is thick enough for the feed from the driver, and keep that cable as short as possible by placing the driver close to the sign.
markingPoints: Defines voltage drop as voltage lost along a conductor due to resistance
Notices: far end dimmer or colour changes
Keeps runs within the maker's maximum length / feeds at both ends or along the run
Uses 24 V instead of 12 V for lower current
Uses thick enough, short feed cables, with the driver near the sign

essays.stem: Describe how to work safely at height when fixing an LED sign above a public sidewalk.
essays.modelAnswer: Choose the right access equipment for the height and the job. A mobile scaffold or work platform is safer than a ladder for long jobs; a ladder is only for short, light work. Check the equipment before use for damage, and set it on firm, level ground with the wheels locked or the ladder at about 75°, tied or footed. Keep three points of contact on a ladder and do not over-reach. Cone or tape off the sidewalk below and use a person on the ground to keep the public away, because dropped tools or parts can injure people. Carry tools in a belt or haul them up in a bag, and tie off tools where possible. Do not work in strong wind, rain or lightning. Two people should work together so that one can help or raise the alarm. Wear a hard hat, safety glasses and safety boots, and follow the Centre's rules.
markingPoints: Chooses suitable access (scaffold or platform; ladder only for short work)
Inspects equipment; firm, level base; ladder at about 75°, secured; three points of contact
Barriers and a ground person to protect the public
Secures tools and parts against falling
Stops in bad weather; works in pairs; correct PPE

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would take to make the electrical connections of an outdoor LED sign weatherproof.
essays.modelAnswer: Choose parts rated for outdoor use: LED modules and a driver with a suitable IP rating, and UV-resistant cable and ties. Bring cables into boxes from below or from the side, never through the top, using a cable gland of the right size and tightening it so that it grips the cable. Leave a drip loop in each cable just before the entry, so water runs off the low point. Make joints inside a rated junction box or with the maker's sealed connectors, not with tape. Fill unused holes with proper blanking plugs. Where the maker allows, drill small drain holes at the lowest point of the sign box so any water can escape. Seal round the fixings and entries with a suitable outdoor sealant. Finally, check every lid and gasket is seated and closed tightly before the sign is powered.
markingPoints: Uses outdoor-rated (IP) and UV-resistant parts
Cable entries from below or the side through sized, tightened glands
Drip loops before entries
Joints in rated boxes or sealed connectors; blanks in unused holes
Drainage and sealant as the maker allows; lids and gaskets closed

essays.stem: Explain, in order, how to safely isolate the supply to an existing LED sign before replacing its driver.
essays.modelAnswer: First tell the owner and anyone affected that the sign will be switched off. Find the right isolator or circuit breaker from the drawing or the board schedule. Switch it off. Lock it off with your own lock so that nobody can switch it back on, and fix a tag saying who is working and why. Check your voltage tester on a proving unit to show it works. Then test at the driver's supply terminals between every pair: line and neutral, line and earth, neutral and earth, to prove there is no voltage. Check the tester again on the proving unit, to show it did not fail during the test. Only then start work. Keep the key with you. When the job is finished and checked, remove your lock and tag and restore the supply. Never work live.
markingPoints: Identifies the correct isolator and switches off
Locks off and tags it
Checks the tester on a proving unit before testing
Tests between all conductors to prove dead
Rechecks the tester after; never works live

essays.stem: Describe how you would fix a sign box securely to a concrete block wall, and why this matters in Jamaica.
essays.modelAnswer: First check the wall is sound, with no cracks or loose render, and find out whether the blocks are hollow or filled. Mark the fixing positions from the sign's template or bracket, using a tape and a spirit level so the sign will hang straight. Check with a detector that no cables or pipes are behind the marks. Wearing safety glasses and a dust mask, drill the holes with a hammer drill and a masonry bit of the size the fixing maker states, to the right depth, and blow or brush out the dust. Fit masonry anchors or bolts of the type and size the maker states, enough of them to carry the weight and wind load, and tighten them to the stated torque. Check the sign is level and does not move. This matters in Jamaica because hurricanes and strong winds can tear off a badly fixed sign and throw it onto people or cars.
markingPoints: Checks the wall is sound and the type of block
Marks positions level using a template, tape and spirit level; checks for hidden services
Drills to the maker's size and depth with PPE; cleans holes
Uses the stated masonry fixings, enough for weight and wind, tightened properly
Explains hurricane and wind risk to the public

essays.stem: Describe how a new LED sign is tested and commissioned before it is handed over to the customer.
essays.modelAnswer: Testing starts with the supply off. Check every connection is tight and matches the wiring diagram. Use a meter to check that the DC output wiring has no short circuit between + and −, and that the polarity at each module is right. Check that the metal frame is connected to earth. The mains side of the driver is tested by a qualified person, including an insulation resistance test and a check of the earth and the protective device, as the Centre's rules and the job's rules require. Then the authorised person switches on. Check that every module lights evenly and that there are no dark or dim sections. Measure the voltage at the far end of each run to check voltage drop. Test the photocell or time switch. Finally, record the readings, label the isolator and driver, and show the customer how to use the controls and whom to call.
markingPoints: Dead checks first: connections against the diagram, no short circuit, correct polarity
Earth continuity to the metal frame
Mains-side tests done by a qualified/authorised person; authorised person switches on
Function test: even light, voltage at far end, controls work
Records results, labels, and hands over to the customer

essays.stem: Compare four types of LED sign: channel letters, lightboxes, LED strip outlines and programmable message displays. Say what each is and where each is best used.
essays.modelAnswer: Channel letters are separate hollow letters, usually metal or plastic with an acrylic face, each lit from inside by LED modules. They look smart and are seen from far away, so they suit shop and company names on a building front. A lightbox is a box with a printed acrylic or fabric face lit evenly from behind by LED modules. It is cheaper than channel letters and suits smaller shops, menus and signs at the roadside. An LED strip outline uses flexible LED strip or neon-style LED tube fixed round the edge of a sign, window or building to draw attention, as on bars and restaurants. A programmable message display is a panel of many LEDs controlled by a computer board, so it can show changing words, prices and pictures. It suits pharmacies, gas stations and churches that want to change messages often.
markingPoints: Channel letters: separate letters lit inside; building names
Lightbox: face lit from behind; cheaper; small shops and menus
Strip outline: flexible strip round edges; draws attention
Message display: programmable panel; changing text, prices
A sensible place of use for each

essays.stem: Half of a customer's LED sign has stopped lighting. Describe how you would find and fix the fault safely.
essays.modelAnswer: First ask the customer what happened, for example after rain or a storm. Look at the sign from the ground for damage, water inside or a loose cable. Then isolate the supply: switch off, lock off, tag and prove dead with a checked tester. Open the sign and check for burnt or wet connections, a loose wire or a corroded connector at the start of the dark section. Since half of the sign still works, the driver is probably working, so the fault is likely in the wiring or connector to the dark half, or a failed module at the start of that run. Check continuity of the feed wires with a meter. Repair or replace the faulty connector, wire or module with the same type, and seal it properly. Then close the sign, have the supply restored, and check that the whole sign lights evenly. Record what was found and done.
markingPoints: Gathers information and makes a visual check
Isolates safely before opening the sign
Reasons that the driver works, so checks wiring/connectors/first module of the dark section
Uses a meter for continuity; repairs with like-for-like parts and reseals
Restores supply, tests the whole sign and records the work

practical1.title: Assemble and wire a backlit LED sign panel
practical1.brief: As a group, build a small backlit sign panel (about 600 mm × 400 mm) on a backboard. Lay out the LED modules evenly from the instructor's drawing, fix them with screws or the maker's adhesive, and wire them in the groups the drawing shows, using the correct polarity and the maker's connectors. Bring the DC feed to a terminal block marked as the driver's output, with a cable gland and a drip loop where it enters. Do not connect any driver to the mains: the driver's mains side is not part of this task. With the board dead, check every connection, the polarity and for short circuits with a meter, and record the readings. The assessor then connects a 12 V DC bench supply to the terminal block and switches it on. Measure the voltage at the first and last module. Each member lays out and fixes some modules, makes at least one connection, and takes one meter reading. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Backboard (plywood or aluminium sheet), about 600 mm × 400 mm
12 V DC LED modules with the maker's connectors and data sheet
Two-core flexible cable, cable ties and clips
Terminal block, small enclosure and cable gland
12 V DC bench supply, connected and switched by the assessor
photos: The layout marked out on the backboard from the drawing
The modules fixed in place, evenly spaced
The wiring finished, showing polarity and clipped cables
The gland and drip loop at the terminal enclosure
The meter check for short circuits with the board dead
The panel lit evenly on the bench supply, with the far-end voltage reading
checklist: Marked out and spaced the modules evenly as the drawing shows
Fixed modules firmly by the maker's method
Made connections with correct polarity using the maker's connectors
Fitted the gland correctly and left a drip loop
Checked for short circuits and polarity with the board dead and recorded readings
Measured and recorded the voltage at the first and last module
Kept cables neat and clipped, with no strain on joints
Worked safely and helped leave the area clean
safety: No mains is used: only the assessor connects and switches the 12 V DC bench supply
Switch off before changing any wiring
Wear safety glasses when cutting cable ties and drilling
Keep tools and off-cuts off the floor to prevent trips

practical2.title: Mount an LED sign box and strip outline on a training wall
practical2.brief: As a group, fix a small sign box to the Centre's training wall (concrete block, or a timber frame if no block wall is free) at about 2 m high, then fit an LED strip outline round it and wire it ready for power. Plan the job first: mark the fixing positions level, check for hidden services, and set out the access equipment. Use a podium step or a stepladder at the right angle, with one member footing it and one keeping the area clear. Drill and fit masonry fixings as the maker states, and check the box is level. Fix the LED strip round the box, cutting only at the marked lines, and feed power in at both ends from a junction box, with the cable entering from below through a gland and with a drip loop. The assessor checks the set-up, then connects a 12 V or 24 V DC bench supply (to suit the strip) and switches it on. Measure the voltage at the middle of the run. Each member takes a turn at drilling or fixing, wiring, and footing the steps or guarding the area. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Small sign box or lightbox (training sample)
Masonry fixings and a hammer drill with masonry bits
Spirit level, tape measure, pencil and a cable and pipe detector
LED strip (12 V or 24 V DC) with the maker's connectors and data sheet
Weatherproof junction box, cable glands, two-core cable and UV-resistant ties
12 V or 24 V DC bench supply, connected and switched by the assessor
photos: Fixing positions marked level on the wall, with the detector check
Access equipment set up and footed, with the area taped off
The sign box fixed and checked with a spirit level
The LED strip fixed round the box, with both feed points
The junction box entry from below with gland and drip loop
The outline lit on the bench supply, with the mid-run voltage reading
checklist: Marked the fixing positions level and checked for hidden services
Set up and used the steps safely, or footed them for others
Drilled and fitted fixings as the maker states, wearing safety glasses and a dust mask
Fixed the box level and secure
Cut and joined the strip only at the marked points, with correct polarity
Fed power at both ends and made a weatherproof entry with a gland and drip loop
Took and recorded a voltage reading
Cleaned up dust and off-cuts and stored the steps
safety: Only the assessor connects and switches the DC bench supply; no mains is used
Use steps at the right angle on firm ground, keep three points of contact, and do not over-reach
Wear safety glasses and a dust mask when drilling; check for hidden cables and pipes first
Keep the area below the work taped off and free of people
